predict.question: In a 45 °C fanless (0 LFM) M.2 2280 slot, what happens to junction temperature T_J on a Numato Aller A7 (XC7A200T-2FBG484C) at 250 MHz if onboard DDR3 800 MT/s and PCIe Gen2 x4 are left active instead of running purely from RAMB36E1?

choices.label: T_J stays near 55.2 est_C because the 4 KB LUT6 core uses 0 DSP48E1 slices
choices.why: 55.2 est_C requires holding DDR3 in CMOS reset, trimming PCIe to Gen2 x1, and mounting the passive heatsink; MIG PHY + DDR3 + 4 GTP lanes add +1,395 mW of non-compute heat.

choices.label: T_J plateaus at 78.0 est_C because 28nm static leakage stays constant above 45 °C
choices.why: 28nm HPL core/BRAM static leakage rises exponentially with T_J (DS181: 486.9 mW at 85 °C), amplifying self-heating in a bare 22x80 mm M.2 slot.

choices.label: T_J climbs to 95.8 est_C (2.55 est_W on M.2 3.3V), breaching the 85 °C commercial limit
choices.why: Exact match (AMD DS181 + UG475 coupled fixed-point)! MIG 7-Series PHY (680 mW), DDR3 (330 mW), and 4 GTP lanes (640 mW) drive M.2 3.3V draw to 2.55 est_W and T_J to 95.8 est_C.

labs.title: From Ephemeral Inference to Compiled Agency: Sub-Bit Impedance Tax, waiOS Tamper Halt & the 4-Stage Cascade
labs.subtitle: Audit the 81.86× KV260 INA260 FP32 unpack penalty, inject a Row-77 single-weight tamper to trigger waiOS BLAKE3 halt, and engage Packed Integer + the 4-Stage Cascade for a 26.58× gross (24.49× net) shunt cut.
labs.key_concept: Compressing a 512×512 matrix 52.72× to 0.1517 bits/weight (4,972 B) and unpacking to FP32 at runtime burns 63,335.56 µJ gross (3,813.32 µJ net)—an 81.86× gross (71.91× net) impedance penalty over dense INT8 (773.74 µJ) on Kria KV260 TI INA260 (measured_j); staying in Packed Integer (FWHT + XNOR + popcount + 4-bit LUT: 187.49 µJ, 4.13× below INT8), guarding Stage 3 with 4-ISA waiOS BLAKE3 lockstep (a541323b…46f0, Row-77 tamper -> 4ac7c4fb…69dc HALT), and routing via the 4-Stage Lookup-First Cascade cuts KV260 INA260 measured_j by 26.58× gross (24.49× net) and Jetson Thor INA3221 by 16.26× while avoiding 38.46× Stage-4 escalations.

predict.question: When a 512×512 weight matrix is compressed 52.72× to 0.1517 bits/weight (4,972 B) and unpacked to FP32 at runtime on AMD Kria KV260 (TI INA260 SOM 5V DC shunt measured_j), how does energy per correct decision compare to dense INT8 (773.74 µJ)?

choices.label: 14.68 µJ gross (~52.72× lower than dense INT8, scaling linearly with byte footprint)
choices.why: Byte footprint alone ignores execution impedance: unpacking 0.1517 bpw codes back into FP32 on every query burns 18.18 ms of bit-unpacking and float MACs on Cortex-A53.

choices.label: ~773.74 µJ gross (~1.00× parity with dense INT8 because 4,972 B fits in L1 cache)
choices.why: L1 residency saves DRAM traffic, not per-query FP32 decompression work—only staying in Packed Integer (187.49 µJ gross, 10.30 µJ net, 4.13× below INT8) eliminates the unpack loop.

choices.label: 63,335.56 µJ gross (3,813.32 µJ net) — an 81.86× gross (71.91× net) decompression impedance penalty!
choices.why: Exact match (openIE-dev/openie-research-experiments @ 813eb96, N=8, 0.11% idle drift)! Runtime FP32 unpacking turns a 52.72× storage win into an 81.86× gross (71.91× net) INA260 energy penalty unless compute stays in Packed Integer (187.49 µJ gross, 10.30 µJ net).

steps.goal: Trigger Naive FP32 + Always-Dense energy spike or Row-77 waiOS BLAKE3 HALT

steps.prompt: Switch Kernel to 'Packed Integer (FWHT + XNOR + popcount + 4-bit LUT)', clear 'Row-77 Tamper' (a541323b…46f0 restored), and activate '4-Stage Spellcheck Lookup-First Cascade' (Zipf s = 0.85..1.15, d_max = 2, τ = 4500), cutting KV260 INA260 measured_j by 26.58× gross (24.49× net) (16.26× on Jetson Thor INA3221) and avoiding 38.46× Stage-4 escalations!
steps.goal: Seal BLAKE3 a541323b…46f0 with Packed Integer + 4-Stage Cascade (s=0.85..1.15, d_max=2, τ=4500)

labs.title: Goodhart Spec-Fidelity Barrier & Wasm Fuel vs. Physical Joules
labs.subtitle: Defeat 99.50% (199/200) Goodhart false accepts via Spec ⊥ Impl + 100% AST Mutant Kill + In-Loop Grammar Masking, and calibrate identical 330,000,004 Wasmtime 50.0.1 fuel against a 10.36× DRAM RAPL joule gap.
labs.key_concept: Measured @ d036b64 (Signed Provenance · Self-Checked): an LLM's own shared-context test (assert len(out) == len(inp)) falsely admits 199/200 (99.50%) AST mutants until Spec ⊥ Impl + 100% AST Mutant/Vacuity Kill Gate cuts false accepts to 0/200 (0.00%, 95% Clopper–Pearson [0.0000, 0.0183]) and In-Loop Grammar Masking eliminates 100% of syntax waste (298,175 -> 0 tokens, 45.22× lower Zen 5 RAPL reported_j); meanwhile, identical 330,000,004 Wasmtime 50.0.1 fuel diverges 10.36× in CLI RAPL reported_j (14.00 J 64 MiB DRAM vs. 1.35 J L1 ALU), requiring orthogonal OTel reported_j/measured_j spans + 144.7 B RFC 9052 COSE_Sign1 receipts.

predict.question: Suppose a ~70 µs gate checks an LLM's own shared-context test (assert len(out) == len(inp)) against 200 broken sorting/ledger AST mutants, AND two Wasmtime 50.0.1 loops burn identical 330,000,004 instruction fuel (L1 ALU vs. 64 MiB DRAM thrash). What happens?

choices.label: 0% false accepts and 1.00× equal physical joules (fast tests catch logic bugs, and Wasm fuel equals energy)
choices.why: Both fail empirically (@ d036b64): an LLM-authored shape check falsely accepts 199/200 (99.50%) broken AST mutants, and 64 MiB DRAM thrashing burns 10.36× more Linux RAPL reported_j (14.00 J vs. 1.35 J) at identical 330,000,004 Wasmtime fuel!

choices.why: Context isolation alone (Arm B) still falsely accepts 146/200 (73.00%) mutants when partial specs omit boundary invariants, and DRAM cache misses multiply energy per Wasm instruction by ~10× (9.80× in-process, 10.36× CLI)!

choices.label: 99.50% (199/200) Goodhart false accepts on shared specs AND a 10.36× RAPL reported_j gap (14.00 J vs. 1.35 J) at 1.000000× equal fuel!
choices.why: Exact match (@ d036b64, Kits #8 & #9)! Closing Goodhart's loophole requires Spec ⊥ Impl + 100% AST Mutant/Vacuity Kill Gate (0/200 false accepts), and Wasmtime fuel enforces deterministic termination (trapping at 330,000,003) while OTel reported_j/measured_j records physical energy.
